title: A Glucose Trend Line Moves Onto the Camera Feed Itself | vitalii.no
description:
Artem's 24-hour glucose trend used to live only inside his own CareLink app. The kiosk TV in the room showed his current number on a photo badge, but nobody could tell whether that number had gone up or down through the day without unlocking a phone. The first attempt at a fix, a full chart under the calendar, ate so much screen space and colour that it fought for attention instead of helping.

I added a component that draws Artem's last 24 hours directly over the bottom fifth of his own camera feed instead of claiming a calendar row. The line is coloured per point — white inside the healthy range, red below it, yellow above — with the limits drawn as thin dashed guides and hour marks along the axis. It pulls fresh history on the same five-minute cadence the source app itself updates, and deliberately drops the big current-value readout an earlier pass added, since that number already lives on Artem's photo badge; the chart only needs to show the shape of the day.

It took four full redesigns in one evening — chart under the calendar, camera overlay, recolour for a white background, hour and limit labels — before the layout finally landed.
